recipes.name: Heart-Healthy Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in soluble fiber from oats and vegetables, which helps lower LDL cholesterol. It's a low-fat, nutrient-dense breakfast.
instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat rice bran oil. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté for a minute.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add mixed vegetables and turmeric powder. Cook for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add water and salt, bring it to a boil. Once boiling, add the roasted oats gradually, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes, or until all water is absorbed and oats are cooked.
Switch off the flame, stir in lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Lean Chicken and Palak Stir-fry
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein for satiety and muscle maintenance, iron from spinach, and is low in saturated fat, supporting healthy cholesterol levels. Also offers Vitamin D benefits if chicken is from fortified sources.
instructions: Marinate chicken strips with a pinch of salt, turmeric, and black pepper for 10 minutes.
Heat rice bran oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and green chili (if using). Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions and cook until translucent. Add chicken strips and cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through.
Stir in cumin powder and coriander powder. Sauté for another minute until fragrant.
Add sliced capsicum and chopped spinach. Cook until spinach wilts and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Season with salt to taste. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the stir-fry before serving. Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Vitamin D Rich Grilled Fish with Steamed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Fatty fish like mackerel or pomfret are excellent sources of Omega-3 fatty acids, which help lower triglycerides, and Vitamin D, crucial for bone health and immune function. Low-fat cooking method further supports heart health.
instructions: Wash and pat dry the fish fillet. In a bowl, mix ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, cumin powder, half of the chopped coriander leaves, juice from half a lemon, and salt to taste. Marinate the fish with this mixture for at least 15 minutes.

Preheat a grill pan or oven. Lightly brush the grill pan with olive oil. Place the marinated fish on the hot grill. Grill for 4-6 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until cooked through and flaky.
While the fish is grilling, steam the broccoli florets and carrot slices until tender-crisp (about 5-7 minutes).
Serve the grilled fish immediately with the steamed vegetables. Garnish with remaining coriander leaves and a lemon slice.

recipes.name: High-Fiber Chana Masala (Nut-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: Chickpeas are an excellent source of soluble fiber, which is crucial for binding cholesterol in the digestive tract and helping to lower LDL. This recipe is made without nuts and with minimal oil, making it heart-healthy.
instructions: Heat rice bran oil in a kadai or heavy-bottomed pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the masala.
Add boiled chickpeas, chana masala powder, dry mango powder, and salt. Mix well. Add about 1 cup of water (or as needed for desired consistency).
Cover and simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Mash a few chickpeas with the back of your spoon to thicken the gravy.
Stir in garam masala and half of the chopped coriander leaves. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Garnish with remaining coriander leaves. Serve hot with whole wheat rotis or brown rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad (Chaat Style)
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong dal provides easily digestible protein and a high amount of fiber, contributing to lower LDL and overall digestive health. It's a light, refreshing, and nutrient-dense snack.
instructions: If not pre-sprouted, soak moong dal overnight, then drain and keep in a moist cloth in a warm place for 1-2 days until sprouts appear.
Lightly steam the sprouted moong dal for 5-7 minutes or boil briefly to remove raw taste, then drain and cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled sprouted moong dal with chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, green chili (if using), and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, black salt, and roasted cumin powder. Mix everything gently until well combined.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Serve immediately as a refreshing and healthy snack.

recipes.name: Masala Omelette with Mushrooms and Spinach
recipes.health_benefit: Eggs provide high-quality protein and some natural Vitamin D in the yolk. Mushrooms are one of the few plant sources of Vitamin D (especially if UV-treated). Spinach adds fiber and micronutrients, making this a nutritious and filling breakfast supporting Vitamin D and overall health.
instructions: In a bowl, whisk eggs with salt, black pepper, and turmeric powder.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
Add sliced mushrooms and chopped spinach. Cook until mushrooms are tender and spinach has wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Pour the whisked egg mixture over the vegetables in the pan. Sprinkle with green chili (if using) and chopped coriander leaves.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the edges set. Gently fold the omelette in half or cook until set to your preference.
Serve hot, perhaps with a slice of whole-wheat toast.

recipes.name: Nut-Free Lauki Chana Dal (Bottle Gourd & Chickpea Lentil)
recipes.health_benefit: Lauki (bottle gourd) is a low-calorie, high-fiber vegetable. Chana dal provides plant-based protein and soluble fiber, which collectively help manage LDL cholesterol and improve satiety, all within a nut-free Indian preparation.
instructions: Drain the soaked chana dal. In a pressure cooker, add chana dal, diced lauki, turmeric powder, and 1.5 cups of water. Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles or until dal is tender but not mushy.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Once cumin seeds splutter, add chopped onion and sauté until light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Sauté for a minute until raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomato, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and the masala thickens.
Add the cooked dal and lauki mixture to the pan. Add remaining water if needed to adjust consistency. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in garam masala and salt. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing flavors to combine.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with whole wheat rotis or brown rice.

lifestyle_advice: **Consistent Physical Activity:** Continue with your moderately active lifestyle. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity exercise per week, combined with strength training twice a week, to support cardiovascular health and overall well-being.

**Regular Sun Exposure:** To help improve Vitamin D levels naturally, aim for 10-15 minutes of direct sun exposure (e.g., arms and legs exposed) during midday, several times a week, while being mindful of skin protection to avoid sunburn.
**Stress Management:** Incorporate stress-reducing activities such as meditation, yoga, deep breathing exercises, or hobbies you enjoy. Chronic stress can impact various health markers.
**Adequate Sleep:** Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night. Sufficient sleep is vital for hormone regulation, recovery, and overall health.
**Hydration:** Drink plenty of water throughout the day (around 8-10 glasses) to support metabolic functions, aid digestion, and maintain energy levels.

**Regular Health Monitoring:** Work closely with your healthcare provider to regularly monitor your LDL cholesterol, Vitamin D levels, and other relevant biomarkers to track progress and make any necessary adjustments to your nutrition and lifestyle plan.
